stage1_evidence_shown.label: OBJECTIVE
stage1_evidence_shown.context: To determine if composite measures based on process indicators are consistent with short-term outcome indicators in surgical colorectal cancer care.

stage1_evidence_shown.label: DESIGN
stage1_evidence_shown.context: Longitudinal analysis of consistency between composite measures based on process indicators and outcome indicators for 85 Dutch hospitals.

stage1_evidence_shown.label: SETTING
stage1_evidence_shown.context: The Dutch Surgical Colorectal Audit database, the Netherlands.

stage1_evidence_shown.label: PARTICIPANTS
stage1_evidence_shown.context: 4732 elective patients with colon carcinoma and 2239 with rectum carcinoma treated in 85 hospitals were included in the analyses.

stage1_evidence_shown.label: MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES
stage1_evidence_shown.context: All available process indicators were aggregated into five different composite measures. The association of the different composite measures with risk-adjusted postoperative mortality and morbidity was analysed at the patient and hospital level.

stage2_added_evidence.label: RESULTS
stage2_added_evidence.context: At the patient level, only one of the composite measures was negatively associated with morbidity for rectum carcinoma. At the hospital level, a strong negative association was found between composite measures and hospital mortality and morbidity rates for rectum carcinoma (p<0.05), and hospital morbidity rates for colon carcinoma.
